speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY).

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But we certainly do not live in quiet times today.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The world around us is very much unsettled.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Major powers are contesting influence across regions and supply chains.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Closer to home, regional tensions periodically flare as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For a small and open country like ours, these developments are not distant headlines.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They are reminders that the global environment is becoming more fragmented and uncertain.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In such a world, national resilience cannot rest only on economic strength or military capability.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It must also rest on something less visible but equally vital and that is social trust – the confidence that fellow citizens will stand together when it matters.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is the essence of what we mean when we speak about a "we first" society.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But building such a society today is not so straightforward.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Workers are adapting to technological disruption and economic uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In a fast-paced and demanding society, it is natural for people to focus first on their own households.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet if everyone looks only inward, the invisible threads that hold a nation together will loosen.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A "we first" national identity cannot be built by slogans alone.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It cannot rely only on campaigns or occasional events.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It must be experienced in daily life and reinforced through habits.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Surveys by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) consistently show relatively high levels of trust in our public institutions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Community participation and volunteering have grown steadily over the years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These are among the highest levels of social trust anywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Such trust did not arise by accident, of course.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It refers to a vibrant culture of associations where citizens organise sports clubs, cultural groups and volunteer initiatives.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of these organisations are run not by professionals but by ordinary citizens.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These associations build horizontal bonds across age, profession and background.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They create the social networks that sustain trust.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This word has no perfect English translation, but it captures a sense of warmth, togetherness and shared belonging.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It reflects the idea that communal life matters, that it is not merely a collection of individuals pursuing individual goals.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These examples remind us that social cohesion is not automatic.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, for us, we must begin with our young.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Schools are places where students prepare for life.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They are also where civic instincts are formed.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Programmes that bring students into contact with different segments of society can deepen empathy and a sense of shared responsibility.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In workplaces, many Singaporeans spend a large part of their lives at work.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Employers therefore have an opportunity to foster environments where collaboration across backgrounds, nationalities and skills is valued and where corporate volunteering helps employees contribute beyond their professional roles.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In our neighbourhoods as well, those are the most immediate setting where "we first" instincts can flourish.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore's housing model has long been a quiet but powerful engine of social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But as lifestyles change, we need to reinforce face-to-face engagements so that neighbours do not become strangers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Initiatives that bring residents together can help restore that sense of familiarity with each other.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must recognise that much of our national conversation takes place online.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But they also amplify outrage, misinformation and polarisation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, for a diverse and multicultural society like ours, cultivating digital citizenship is also essential.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our online spaces must reflect the same values of responsibility and mutual respect as we do in our physical spaces.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must also continue to bridge differences across generations and socioeconomic groups between the old and the young.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Creating opportunities for these generations to interact will help anchor our national identity in both memory and renewal.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must guard against social silos forming as economic pressures rise.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A "we first" society must ensure that compassion and mutual support remain embedded within our social compact.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, therefore, I look forward to hearing how MCCY intends to further embed the ethos of "we first" across multiple aspects of society so that our national identity is formed through participation, not just persuasion.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It will be the quiet but enduring conviction amongst our people that our fate is shared, and that when the world is more turbulent, Singaporeans will instinctively do what we have always done best – to put "we" before "me".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because in this uncertain world, the greatest strength Singapore possesses will not just be our economy or institutions, but our people.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   Our young people face a lot of pressure – school, exams, social media.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Many are quietly asking themselves: "Who am I and where do I belong?" When stress, identity and belonging collide, our mosques can be more than just places of worship.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Mosques can be powerful partners for youth well-being, because they offer community, meaning, trusted adult that provide guidance.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For many youths, struggles with anxiety or identity are not just emotional questions.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Involve them in sustained youth co-design at district and congregational levels, so programmes speak to real challenges youth face.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: When a young person is struggling, they may approach an ustaz or a youth leader long before they approach formal services.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Spiritual guidance and professional care must work hand-in-hand.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We cannot wait for youths to walk through the doors of the mosque.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Bring mentoring and resilience workshops into community spaces and digital platforms.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Every young Malay/Muslim deserves to know: they are seen, they are valued, they are supported – in faith and in life.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: When our youths are anchored in faith and supported in well-being, our community – and our nation – are stronger.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
text: How will SCIS ensure that its programmes will maintain high standards of Islamic scholarship relative to other institutions around the world, with the aim of producing graduates who not only contribute to the needs of the Muslim community but extend their depth of scholarly knowledge, wisdom and expertise to also benefit wider Singapore society and indeed, the world as a whole?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
text: How does the Minister see SCIS' importance, centrality and development in the context of today's global developments and SCIS' potential contributions alongside Singapore's nation building efforts and forward aspirations as a country?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, in January, I asked a Parliamentary Question about the population planning parameters used to determine whether a new mosque will be built, and whether these parameters include not only Muslim residents, but also the daytime Muslim working population and Muslim foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: The Minister's answer did not reveal the specific population planning parameter or the exact mosque-to-Muslim-resident ratio, that the Government uses.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: My question was prompted by the planned closure of Masjid Al-Firdaus in Choa Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Although located in an isolated area, this mosque has served the spiritual needs of the community, including National Servicemen stationed nearby and foreign workers employed in the area, for more than 60 years.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: This raises the question: what are the specific planning parameters to determine whether and when a mosque should be closed down, relocated, expanded or newly built?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Moreover, while we rely on planning parameters to determine how many mosques to build, we must also consider heritage beyond numbers.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: For example, because of historical settlement patterns, we still have kampung-style mosques in sparsely populated areas, like Masjid Omar Salmah in Bukit Brown or Masjid Hang Jebat in Queenstown.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: These mosques may no longer have large congregations but still have long histories that carry meaning for the community.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: When new housing estates are built, will it be the policy to rationalise the number of mosques by relocating or closing old mosques, like Masjid Al-Firdaus?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: As the Minister noted, mosques are funded by the community through the Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund (MBMF).

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Mosques have always been community resources and anchors of faith, history and identity, built through sacrifice and collective effort.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: How can we strike a better balance between prudent urban planning with heritage preservation?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: WMS has the potential to become the financial backbone supporting the SCIS, ensuring the continuity of our madrasahs and covering the operating and leasing costs of our mosques.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Beyond funding institutions and infrastructure, WMS funds are expected to flow toward social support programmes, education and youth development – investments that will shape the character and capability of future generations.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Without adequate contributions, we risk compromising the very institutions and programmes that preserve our religious heritage and nurture our community's potential.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: WMS offers every Muslim in Singapore the opportunity to create this perpetual legacy, where there may be constrains to pledge other forms of Waqaf.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Every contribution becomes a seed that continuously bears fruit – supporting students, sustaining places of worship and uplifting those in need.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: I propose that we significantly expand community engagement through diverse platforms: mosques, community centres, schools, professional associations and student societies.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: These sessions should empower our community with knowledge of the potential profound spiritual and social impact of WMS.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our community is beautifully diverse – Indian/Muslims, Chinese/Muslims, Arab/Muslims, Malay/Muslims, youth, professionals and seniors.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Each group has unique perspectives and preferred communication channels.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Will there be targeted programmes that resonate with their specific contexts?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: When the community sees tangible evidence of the funds being used responsibly – that a student has graduated, a family has been supported, a mosque has been maintained – it reinforces trust and inspires others to follow suit.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: From 150 contributors to thousands – this must be our trajectory.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Every Muslim family should consider WMS in their legacy planning, not as an obligation, but as an opportunity to invest in eternity.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, I want to address challenges facing many young families.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many belong to the "sandwich generation" and face pressure from rising cost of living, while balancing responsibilities of raising children and caring for aging parents.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Sometimes, they bear all this without strong family support networks, unlike previous generations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a mother, I have went through the early stages of marriage and parenthood that was filled with joy.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But when facing new experiences, feelings of confusion, fear and exhaustion may emerge.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Preparing breakfast, adjusting to new routines, staying up when the child is crying – all while balancing work and family demands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, the Bersamamu Programme and Project ARIF have helped many young couples in early marriage and parenthood, providing religious guidance, medical perspectives and practical skills like financial planning.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, can we consider strengthening collaboration with programmes like KidSTART so family support can be implemented continuously?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will Government increase its outreach and ensure young couples know about these programmes?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With an increasing number of multi-generational families and seniors, our social landscape is clearly changing.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have often advocated on the need to focus on our seniors.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the national level, there are many efforts supporting seniors in their golden years.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But can we consider support programmes for multi-generational families living under one roof and our seniors?

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: While we understand that most of the funds are set aside for education, it is important to recognise that the finances within this organisation is still robust.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: We need to look beyond education as the sole pathway to success and explore other forms of achievement, like the arts, sports and career development.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: We want to ensure that every individual receives the necessary support and becomes the best version of themselves.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: MENDAKI should also look into providing holistic support to families that encompasses financial literacy education and strengthening family bonds.

speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
text: MENDAKI should be able to envision how this community can be developed and ensure that the programmes designed to support it are implemented holistically and professionally.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, part of our AI transformation strategy must ensure that our children and youth are equipped not only to use technology, but are also able to create value with it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Toa Payoh recently, I met a Secondary 4 student who told me he was interested in AI.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, when asked further, he said he had never coded before and was not sure how to start.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What he lacked was not aspiration, but exposure and guidance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many of our seniors are supported by their children and grandchildren who provide companionship, financial help and daily assistance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But as family structures evolve and working lives become more demanding, we should ask how do we sustainably support our seniors' social and mental well-being?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the ground, we see seniors who are widowed and living alone, elderly parents who hesitate to burden their children, or caregivers quietly managing both work and eldercare responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many of them do not openly express their difficulties.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is why social and emotional support must go beyond the occasional event.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It must be sustained, trusted and easily accessible.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we bring back that "kampong spirit" amidst today's modern housing environment?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there accessible support networks and early intervention channels to prevent caregiver burnout?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third, aside from the number of programme attendees, what indicators do we use to measure actual impact – like reduced isolation, improved emotional wellbeing and stronger inter-generational engagement?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: (In Malay):  (In Malay): Mr Chairman, our young people are the hope for our community's future.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The MENDAKI Tuition Programme has greatly helped our students succeed in their studies.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: However, our children's future cannot depend on tuition alone.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The key question is: are we really preparing our young people for tomorrow's job market?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: New industries, such as technology, AI, engineering and the digital economy are expanding.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: We want to see more of our young people dare to dream, be confident in their abilities and pursue future industries, such as aerospace, AI and cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The Government and community organisations need to have closer partnerships – not only in academic support, but also career exposure, mentorship guidance and real job opportunities.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: At M3@Pasir Ris-Changi, we ran programmes, such as Learning Journey, RobotWars and Hackathons to expose our young people to the skills needed in new industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: However, these efforts need to be expanded further.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: How can these networks also partner schools, MENDAKI Tuition, M3 programmes and youth organisations, so that more young people get early exposure to future industries? :   By 2030, Singapore will become an ageing society.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Many seniors visit the mosque daily – not just to pray, but to also seek peace, support and companionship.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Mosques play a key role in the lives of our community.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Imagine if mosques could work more closely with agencies, such as Health Promotion Board and the Ministry of Health, as well as partners in the financial sector to provide comprehensive health, financial and social support – everything in a place that they trust and are familiar with.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In Pasir Ris-Changi, Masjid Al-Istighfar together with M3 held a talk on Lasting Power of Attorney, conducted health screenings, as well as fitness activities, such as Yallah Run and Move with Mufti to support the well-being of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: My question is: How can mosques work more closely with these agencies to provide religious support as well as comprehensive assistance to congregants? :   Chairman, the economy is evolving rapidly and we cannot simply be observers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: With the establishment of the National AI Council, national AI Mission and AI Champions programme, many new opportunities are opening up.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The question is: are Malay/Muslim businesses ready to step forward into this new world?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, I would like to touch on youths transiting from higher education institutions, the Institute of Education (ITE), polytechnics and universities, to the working world.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This transition is an important occasion in every young person's life.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In a rapidly changing economy, having a certificate or diploma is no longer enough.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our youths need early exposure to growth sectors, an understanding of future skills, as well as closer relations with employers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We want more youths entering good jobs in sectors, such as technology, advanced manufacturing, healthcare and AI-enabled roles, not by chance, but through clear and planned pathways.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A more integrated approach like this can help ensure that our youths understand the available opportunities, build confidence and are ready to face the transition more assuredly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, this effort will be more effective if supported by strong coordination between Ministries, agencies and educational institutions, so that these transition pathways are well-structured, have clear outcomes and can be scaled up if proven effective.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, I seek the Minister's views on: how does the Government plan to strengthen coordination between Ministries, institutes of higher learning and community partners so that this support for youth transition can be implemented more systematically, with measurable outcomes, and help more of our youth enter good jobs in growth sectors?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
text: (In Malay):   Language, tradition and culture are the pillars that strengthen our ethnic identity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
text: These elements shape how we understand and appreciate our respective heritage, and help us find the balance that enables us to build together strength and unity within Singapore's diversity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
text: How can the Malay Heritage Centre continue to enhance awareness, knowledge and appreciation of Malay culture, particularly among young people, while contributing to wider efforts to strengthen social cohesion and our collective efforts in nation-building for the future?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, here in Singapore, we are very fortunate to have strong Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs), Indian/Muslim Organisations (IMOs) and other committed partners.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: But when efforts run in parallel, residents can face repeated touchpoints, gaps between services or a confusing hand-off from one organisation to the other.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This is where the M3 network can play a practical, convening role, strengthening collaborations between MMOs and IMOs and other community partners, so strengths are combined and outreach is more coordinated on the ground.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Could the Minister consider adopting a "no wrong door" approach?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In Malay, please. :   Mr Chairman, I call upon our Malay/Muslim community organisations and grassroots bodies to work hand in hand, rather than operating separately.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Each organisation has its own strengths – some are strong in youth matters, some are strong in family issues, some are strong in education, careers or social services.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If we coordinate our efforts, we can reach out to more people, faster and more effectively.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Let us complement each other, share clear frameworks and contribute according to our respective strengths, so that our community can achieve the vision of becoming the best version of ourselves, confident in our identity and continue contributing to Singapore. : In Tamil, please. :   Mr Chairman, though the Indian/Muslim community is a small one, it has made sustained contributions to our nation building.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: To seek solutions to the issues in our community, a whole-of-community effort is needed.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Whole-of-community effort means that MMOs, IMOs and other community organisations must come together and work in unity to achieve our national objectives.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If we work together, our last-mile outreach will be more precise.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Let us work together in endeavouring that our young people, our families and those in need progress forward together.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Many have high hopes in the success and credibility of SCIS, which is seen as a long-term investment for our community and Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Last month in Parliament, I posed questions to the Acting Minister regarding SCIS and felt encouraged by his clarification that the establishment of SCIS has been well-received by our regional partners.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, to bolster confidence in SCIS, it is essential to share information about the efforts that will ensure its quality, governance and desired outcomes.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, as someone who has served over a decade at PPIS – one of the largest MMOs – and a member of the first cohort of the Tunas programme, I deeply understand, cherish and respect our MMOs and IMOs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The majority of MMOs and IMOs were established before 1965, and have endured to this day – they weathered all storms and stood the test of time.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Each one remains focused on their individual objectives, be it strengthening families and empowering women, supporting workers, nurturing youth or guiding children.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: They are experienced organisations that serve as pillars of community trust.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: MMOs and IMOs are assets to our community.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, they should be prioritised as long-term strategic partners, with their sustainability being given due attention.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, regardless of the operator, whether M3, MMOs/IMOs or social service agencies, the mission remains the same – to enhance the quality of life of our community for a brighter future.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, Singapore's efforts to actively support vulnerable families must continue.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The challenges faced by these families, Mr Chairman, are extremely complex – ranging from financial pressures and health issues to family relationships, employment and even housing matters.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Fortunately, assistance is available from various entities, such as Family Service Centres, Social Service Offices, MMOs, ComLink, Project Dian by M3 and others.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: If coordination exists only on paper, families continue to bear the burden of navigating systems.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: There has to be shared practice standards, clear referral pathways for continuity of care.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Beyond programmes and subsidies, social capital itself matters too.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Community platforms that build social capital, such as professional networks, alumni networks or across community connections, play an important role for social mobility.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: For social mobility to be sustained across generations, we must be intentional to invest beyond services and subsidies, but in social capital to open doors of opportunities.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Chairman, as it is often said in the House these past two weeks: where you start should not determine where you can go.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I will take clarifications after my speech.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, let me say a few words on the situation in the Middle East.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our thoughts and prayers are with the innocent civilians in the affected region.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The fact that these attacks took place during the holy month of Ramadan deepens the pain felt by many.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are closely monitoring the situation together with colleagues from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I had a video call last night with some of our Singaporean students in the Middle East.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They were understandably concerned but are staying calm.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I assured them that their safety and well-being is our top priority.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to stay in close contact with them and render any support we can.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also in touch with the Association of Muslim Travel Agents (AMTAS).

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They have advised their member agencies to help affected Umrah travellers with adjustments to their travel plans when needed.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These recent events are a stark reminder that the peace and harmony we have in Singapore is especially precious, and we cannot take it for granted.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There is a Malay saying: "sehati menghadapi, sepakat membangun," it means to stand united in overcoming challenges and to work together to build a better future.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This has always been a defining strength of all Singaporeans, and particularly of the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It has helped our community achieve remarkable progress over the years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have built stronger marriages and more resilient families.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our children are better educated, and many have found good jobs across different sectors of the economy.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are able to practise our faith, celebrate our culture with pride and live in harmony with friends from other races, religions and cultures.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Despite the progress, I recognise that everyone has a different lived experience.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During my engagements with the community, I also hear concerns about job security.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some have shared difficulties in trying to access help, and others have called for greater support for those struggling in silence.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is crucial that as we move forward, we ensure that nobody gets left behind.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, many have asked me what my vision for the community is.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we might each have different circumstances, I envision a Malay/Muslim community where every member can be the best version of themselves at every stage of their lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I speak not just for myself, but for my fellow Parliamentary colleagues, our Government agencies, our MMOs, IMOs, volunteers and many others who give of themselves generously every day.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Because of them, no member of our community should ever have to walk alone.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: By Moving Forward Together, With One Heart, we can achieve our vision to help every member of our community thrive.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do so through three key pillars.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, we will uplift individuals across all life stages to provide them with opportunities to succeed.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, we will develop trusted religious institutions to enrich our community religious life.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Third, we will nurture a vibrant cultural sector that celebrates our unique Singaporean Malay arts, culture and identity.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, we want to uplift individuals and provide them with opportunities to excel at every life stage.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some are already doing well and with the right inspiration, they can reach even greater heights.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Others may need an extra helping hand to succeed.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin mentioned, strong families are key to this, as they are the bedrock of our community and society.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They nurture values, like responsibility and empathy, shape our identity as a person and build our confidence to navigate life's challenges.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Strong families begin with stable marriages, which is why the Bersamamu programme has been so vital to our Muslim community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They serve as trusted advisors throughout the couple's early marriage years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As an example, Mr Radzi Barian Arlandito and Ms Risa Shigemi, a Singaporean-Japanese couple, have benefited greatly from Bersamamu.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Their Naib Kadi, Ustaz Mohammed Nazim Bin Rahuma Dulla, provided invaluable advice to help them navigate cultural differences, religious practices and family dynamics.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As a mentor to the couple, Ustaz Nazim provided spiritual guidance and connected them with like-minded couples facing similar situations.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These officers will guide couples through the various national and community programmes that best address their needs, including those with dual caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the pilot run of Project ARIF, mothers received integrated support from their Kadi and Naib Kadi as well as the medical social workers and healthcare professionals from KK Women's and Children's Hospital.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This includes those who do not qualify for KidSTART, so that they continue to receive the necessary support.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From marriage guidance to parenting support, we are broadening the continuum of care to foster more resilient families and give our children the best headstart in life.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, we want to provide every child the necessary support and pathways to enable them to seize opportunities for success, regardless of their background.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our community has made significant strides in educational achievement, and investment in education remains a key focus, but I agree with Mr Azhar Othman that we can do more to help every child reach their fullest potential in other areas too.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: That is why MENDAKI's 2030 Workplan, which I recently launched with Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad, goes beyond nurturing confident learners and includes building stronger families, supporting a future-ready workforce and growing a thriving community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise that excellence begins early and at home, which is why MENDAKI has strengthened its suite of programmes to support the parenting journey.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From April this year, parents can look forward to ReadySetLearn (RSL) Roadshows held in the heartlands, providing convenient access to workshops and resources on supporting their children's holistic growth.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A key component of this support is RSL Maths Explorer, formerly KelasMateMatika, which prepares parents to guide their pre-schoolers in numeracy skills and prepare for math in Primary 1.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MENDAKI will expand the efforts and roll out RSL Language Explorer, a reading programme designed to equip parents to nurture early literacy in both English and Malay.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, these programmes will build confidence and strengthen learning, laying the foundation for long-term academic success.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, for children from families facing greater challenges, attending school regularly can be difficult for various reasons, such as when parents work shifts or when they must care for younger siblings at home.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These last-mile gaps prevent them from participating fully in their education, and in turn may affect their holistic development.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are determined to close these gaps by providing the customised support that these children and their families need.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, I am glad that MENDAKI and the Ministry of Education (MOE), with the support of the Ministry of Social and Family Development and MCCY, have embarked on a pilot programme at selected schools at Tampines to strengthen after-school care and support for our children from Malay/Muslim families who need additional help.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For some families and their children, the help needed could be to provide them better nutrition, a study desk at home or alternative childcare arrangements.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For others, it could be connecting them to a trusted mentor who can address motivational issues.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, under this pilot, a MENDAKI Care Advisor will work with each identified child's family, school or other social service professionals to understand their unique needs and develop an individualised care plan for the child.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The partnership between the school and community will provide academic and non-academic support to complement existing school efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This pilot has been launched earlier this year, and I want to thank the participating schools and MENDAKI who have worked tirelessly to make this partnership possible and grassroots advisers Dr Charlene Chen and Acting Minister David Neo, for suggesting this approach to address the needs of students in Tampines who need that additional help.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we ensure that no child gets left behind because of circumstances.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how Malay/Muslim educational initiatives are evolving to prepare our youths for an AI-driven economy, while Mr Sharael Taha asked how MENDAKI can better prepare our children and youths for the future through mentorship and awareness of pathways.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, MENDAKI's Tuition Programme has helped many students improve in their academic journey.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But we cannot rely on tuition alone to prepare our students for the future.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is why MENDAKI has enhanced the programme to the MENDAKI Achievement Programme with two new focus areas.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The first is enrichment, where students will have opportunities to be exposed to programmes in areas, such as AI exploration and robotics.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The second area is engagement, where students will be exposed to various education and career pathways.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will enable more students and parents to be connected to support systems, such as MENDAKI's Professional Networks, to help them make more informed education and career choices.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked how we can support our youths in job transitions.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will create more platforms for our youths to connect and learn from professionals who have succeeded in their chosen fields, as they prepare to enter the workforce.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It also seeks to expand access to career advisory services, skills development pathways and employment opportunities.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These efforts will put our youths on a better footing to make informed decisions about their career pathways and seize opportunities in growth industries.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last October, we launched the Malay/Muslim Youth Taskforce, led by Minister of State Rahayu and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun to hear from our youths their views on career development, identity and values and how they could contribute to society.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through this taskforce, we hope to keep our policies relevant, and our youths invested in Singapore's future.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The taskforce has since appointed 13 youth consultants, who are leaders from diverse fields including entrepreneurship, sports, digital media, technology, religion and the social sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They have lined up a series of Youth Conversations in partnership with M3 agencies and the National Youth Council, which will capture the perspectives of youths on various issues close to their hearts and co-create initiatives in support of the national SG Youth Plan.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I look forward to hearing their views on bringing the community forward at the upcoming M3 Youth Festival in August.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I have spoken in detail about our youths, but we must also remember our seniors who have given so much of themselves to build a better future for us.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Both Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Sharael Taha have asked about how we intend to strengthen holistic support for seniors in our community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We must ensure our seniors continue to thrive in their golden years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our Malay/Muslim seniors shared with me that they are doing well but wish to connect more widely and meaningfully with others.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, ageing well is just as much about companionship, dignity and purpose as it is about health and well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, I was very heartened when Masjid Al-Muttaqin, in collaboration with Ma:een and Muhammadiyah Active Ageing Centre, initiated Santunan Emas, a holistic ground-up effort to provides our seniors and caregivers with religious guidance, social engagement activities and healthcare support.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These mosques also work with partners like the Agency for Integrated Care, National Healthcare Group and the Singapore Hospice Council to reach out to our seniors in nursing homes and hospices.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I recently attended the Santunan Emas roadshow at Masjid Darul Ghufran and witnessed how our mosques, partner agencies and volunteers engage our seniors and their caregivers to support them in different areas of need.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, MUIS will work with Santunan Emas networks at local mosques to identify needs and facilitate partnerships with other community organisations, as well as with healthcare providers to enhance healthcare.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: PA, with its grassroots network, can also rally fellow seniors to serve as befrienders, mentors and active members of the community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This way, we strengthen not only our services, but also the culture of care and dignity for our seniors.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, let me turn to our businesses and workers now.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Prime Minister has outlined comprehensive support measures for businesses in recognition of the challenging economic climate, including a corporate tax rebate.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Budget also provides a booster shot for our businesses and workers to transform for the longer term, including to expand to new markets, to reskill and upskill and to adopt new technologies like AI.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Lower-wage workers, in particular, will benefit from the enhancements to the Progressive Wage Credit and Workfare Skills Support schemes, while workers making a career transition will benefit from the expanded SkillsFuture Level-Up programme.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I encourage our Malay/Muslim enterprises and workers to make good use of these schemes.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how Malay/Muslim businesses can participate meaningfully in the digital and AI economy.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has announced that it intends to harness AI as a strategic advantage.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The pursuit of AI must translate into better outcomes, such as stronger livelihoods and more opportunities, so that our community can progress with confidence in this AI economy.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: That is why we must make upskilling practical and accessible.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, the efforts I have shared reflect our unwavering commitment to uplifting every member of our community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In doing so, we hope that they are able to contribute back to strengthen the entire community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They are not just places of worship, but community hubs that foster spiritual growth and promote wellness, where faith comes alive through collective prayers, learning and service to others.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To stay relevant, our mosques must remain forward-looking and be able to adapt to the evolving needs of our community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked how we plan for the development and closure of mosques.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As I have shared in this House, MUIS takes into consideration key factors that contribute to the demand for prayer spaces, such as projected population changes, as well as land development plans, including the building of new housing estates.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where mosques have heritage value, MUIS will work closely with mosque leaders and agencies to preserve them, including in situations where relocation is necessary.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are committed to ensuring our community's religious needs are sufficiently met as Singapore continues to grow.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond infrastructure, our mosques provide various programmes that encourage community building.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar that our mosques can play a larger role in partnering youths to improve their well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Initiatives, like the NEXTGEN SG Mosque Youth Symposium and mosque dialogue with Mufti, allow our youths to engage our religious leadership on contemporary issues, explore specific concerns of the young and develop ideas to address real issues grounded in faith.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our pastoral care programmes also provide spiritual guidance and support to those facing life's difficulties.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The mosque leaders and youth go out and spend time and that is where they learn from one another.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will look into the useful suggestions that Ms Mariam Jaafar has raised earlier.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our asatizah help the community navigate modern issues, such as social challenges, technological advancements and geopolitical conflicts.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Being an asatizah today requires not just deep religious knowledge, but the ability to connect with people and bridge different communities with wisdom and compassion.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is crucial that our asatizah embody these values, engage with empathy and develop relevant skills to be effective guides to the community in today's complex global landscape.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, this is precisely why we must continue developing our religious leadership, and one of our most significant investments in this area is the SCIS.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Syed Harun asked how we will ensure that SCIS' programmes will maintain high standards of Islamic scholarship while still meeting the needs of the local Muslim community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SCIS will be led by our Mufti and supported by distinguished scholars.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The curriculum will be inter-disciplinary, incorporating social sciences modules to give our future asatizah well-rounded perspectives and boost their employability in the religious and adjacent sectors.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The SCIS campus development at Rochor is also underway.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, our mosques, madrasahs and the SCIS are institutions collectively owned by our community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked for updates on the WMS.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also appointed WMS ambassadors to expand our outreach efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I strongly encourage those with the means to give back to the community, and this will ensure the financial sustainability of our social and religious needs for generations to come.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Only when our religious institutions are strong, are we able to nurture an enriching community religious life.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, our rich Singapore Malay culture and heritage anchor our identity and sense of community and define us as distinctively Singaporean Malay.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I have always enjoyed attending our community's cultural events.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I had the privilege of experiencing Gentarasa SG60 last November.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I was struck by the artistic excellence, passion and dedication of the performers who brought our traditions to life with such authenticity.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our cultural expressions serve as vehicles for storytelling, identity formation and intergenerational connection, helping our young understand their cultural roots while inspiring them to contribute their own creative voices to our evolving cultural narrative.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the heart of our culture and heritage lies the Malay Heritage Centre (MHC) in Kampong Gelam.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Syed Harun asked for an update on the MHC's reopening.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I strongly encourage everyone to join these celebrations.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The revitalised MHC will have an expanded mission that goes beyond its traditional role as a repository of artefacts and exhibits.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will become a vibrant hub that offers a variety of programmes, like festivals for children and youth, regular film screenings and community-driven showcases to take the cultural development and placemaking of Kampong Gelam to the next level.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Central to this expanded role will be the MHC's function in deepening documentation and research on Malay culture and heritage as a resource for practitioners and the community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This unit will work with stakeholders to identify areas of focus and support long-term aid research by academics and community groups.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through this effort, we will ensure our cultural narratives are not just preserved, but actively studied, understood and shared with future generations.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We need living practitioners, like Puan Jumaini Ariff, to keep our traditions alive.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Puan Jumaini is a passionate practitioner of traditional storytelling who never fails to dazzle with her craft.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She speaks fondly of it and shares her hopes for a new generation to continue the tradition of a Penglipur Lara.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As I was speaking, I could remember how she was doing it when I was engaging her.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This initiative embodies our commitment to ensuring cultural knowledge and skills get passed down seamlessly from one generation to the next, culminating in showcases through MHC, where mentees can demonstrate their newly acquired expertise and contribute fresh perspectives to age-old traditions.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When our culture is alive and vibrant, it not only becomes a source of pride for us, but it enriches the multicultural fabric that makes Singapore special.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, I have outlined our plans to strengthen our community across the three pillars.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will uplift individuals by providing them opportunities to succeed at every stage of their lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will enrich our community religious life by developing trusted religious institutions.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: And we will nurture a vibrant cultural sector that celebrates our unique identity.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These goals build on the solid foundation that our community leaders have already established over the years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, M3 brings together MENDAKI, MUIS and the People's Association Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (PA MESRA) to address community issues through focus areas and M3@Towns.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to emphasise greater collaborations between M3 agencies and our community partners as we strategise nationally in each of the focus areas and deliver programmes at the M3@Towns level.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I hope that M3+ will better recognise the specialised knowledge and community links of MMOs, IMOs, informal groups and individual contributors who are already doing excellent work on the ground.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact, this is already being done in some areas.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the M3 Engagement Coordination Office at PA have been working with Jamiyah's Darul Islah Halfway House, Pertapis's Halfway House and PPIS's Rise Above Halfway House to strengthen the rehabilitation and reintegration efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They have facilitated training sessions for over 300 ex-offenders to develop financial and practical skills that will empower them to build sustainable futures for themselves and their families.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the town level, the Association of Muslim Professionals has also worked with M3@Woodlands to conduct a micro business programme to equip budding entrepreneurs with knowledge, such as financial management, business ideation and marketing to build sustainable micro businesses.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of the programme participants, Mr Muhammad Nor Hafiz, was able to transform his seasonal cookie sales into a thriving family business called Chonkery.sg.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MMOs, IMOs and other community partners can tap on a variety of community resources to support these efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Dr Hamid Razak and Ms Hazlina rightly pointed out, many of our MMOs and IMOs also provide services directly to families.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will launch this exciting next phase in April 2026, beginning with an M3+ Networking Session.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some of the ideas include putting together a directory of services that our MMO and IMO partners offer so that our M3 Focus Area leads and M3@Towns can systematically work with these community organisations to identify new opportunities and greater synergies for better programme delivery and to close last-mile gaps.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with this effort, we will continue to develop the next generation of community leaders through the TUNAS programme.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: TUNAS brings together emerging community leaders to build their capabilities through knowledge exchange and networking, developing common projects and mentorship from senior community leaders.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To date, two cohorts of leaders have completed the TUNAS programme.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will welcome the third cohort later this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These TUNAS graduates will help drive M3+ forward by connecting partners, identifying opportunities for collaboration and leading ground efforts so that support reaches those in need more seamlessly.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chaiman, in Malay, please. :   Mr Chairman, my vision for the Malay/Muslim community is for us to move forward together with one heart and a shared purpose.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With the spirit of "Moving Forward Together, With One Heart", we aim to provide opportunities and support so that every individual can be the best version of themselves at every stage of their lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We can achieve this vision through three key pillars.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, by uplifting the social and economic outcomes of the community; second, by strengthening religious institutions and cultivating a vibrant religious life; and third, by nurturing Malay arts, culture and heritage.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In childhood education, the RSL programme will be expanded through roadshows held in the heartlands, while the RSL Language Explorer will be launched to complement the RSL Maths Explorer.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The MENDAKI Achievement Programme will provide students with early exposure to AI and robotics, while MENDAKI's Mentoring Programme will be expanded to include Secondary 1 student, to support students comprehensively in their education journey.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For students who need additional help, I am pleased that MENDAKI and MOE have launched a pilot programme in selected schools in Tampines.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With support from the Ministry of Social and Family Development, MCCY and community partners, we can strengthen after-school care and support, helping students attend school consistently and improve their academic performance.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For our seniors, MUIS and PA will support the Santunan Emas programme and its holistic approach which is crucial in an ageing society.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will provide religious guidance, social engagement activities and healthcare support for seniors and their caregivers.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This programme requires strong partnership with all stakeholders: mosques, community partners, families and Government.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through this collective effort, we can ensure our seniors receive the support they need and lead meaningful lives in their golden years.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also finalising partnerships with Islamic educational institutions in Egypt, Jordan and Morocco.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These efforts aim to produce a pipeline of asatizah who are more capable and ready to guide the community in addressing complex contemporary issues.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will serve as the cultural heartbeat of Singapore's Malay community, bringing together festivals, film screenings and community-based exhibitions, to enliven and enrich Kampong Gelam.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The centre will shape the future direction of our culture, supported by a research unit, with an advisory panel led by Dr Norshahril Saat.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Intangible Cultural Heritage Mentorship Programme was launched to connect practitioners with the young generation.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This programme will run for 10 weeks to ensure our knowledge and traditions continue to be preserved and developed across time.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Therefore, I will launch M3+, to involve MMOs, IMOs, informal groups and individuals who want to contribute more comprehensively.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Each M3@Town and Focus Area will work closely with MMOs and IMOs, informal groups and individuals who aspire to serve the community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Additionally, the TUNAS programme will continue developing the next generation of community leaders through knowledge exchange, networking and mentorship from senior community leaders.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: M3+ represents a continuation of the spirit of cooperation that has long been our community's strength, based on the principle of Moving Forward Together, With One Heart.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Let us move forward, with one heart and strive to be the best version at every stage of our lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, Mdm Latipah Binte Abdul Rahman first joined the Santunan Emas programme as a participant in October 2024 to seek spiritual guidance and social support.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Now, she serves as a volunteer coordinator who organises the welcome committee, prepares refreshments and conducts exercise sessions and craft classes.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The knowledge and experience gained had motivated her to give back to the community.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is the transformation we want to see in every member of our community. : Mr Chairman, I spoke about the recent developments that have unfolded in the Middle East at the beginning of my speech.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During times of global uncertainty, it becomes even more important for us to strengthen the bonds that keep us united.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Singaporeans, we must stand together, support one another and maintain the mutual respect and understanding that define our society.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Throughout this speech, I have shared stories of individuals who embody the spirit of "Bersatu Hati, Maju Bersama", each serving as sources of inspiration in their own right.

speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
