text: Externally, the world order that brought us peace and prosperity is being challenged, reversed and dismantled.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have heard how international relations have become more "my interest first", rather than "how can we prosper together".

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Internally, we face a combination of rapid ageing and fast declining fertility.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister said, it is an existential challenge.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will need to stay open with a carefully managed immigration flow to augment our low birth rate.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Will we choose unity over division, sharing over isolation and equality over discrimination?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is in these uncertain times that the question, "what makes me a Singaporean" becomes even more salient for us, as individuals and as a nation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our national identity, which reflects our core values, our principles and our beliefs, will be what anchors us in a changed world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Only when we are strongly anchored in our collective identity as Singaporeans, can we withstand the tests that will come.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The hon Member Mr Alex Yam spoke about the need for a "we first" national identity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In MCCY, we seek to foster a "we first" society in three ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, we need to expand the common space that we share as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At a basic level, we need to do more to get people to interact, bond and identify with one another.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As Members in this Chamber will remember, we used to bond through shared experiences, whether it is watching local television programmes, like Aksi Mat Yoyo or drama serials like 霧鎖南洋, or just going downstairs to play at the dragon playground.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: With Netflix, YouTube and TikTok, experiences become more individualised.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We can be in the same room at the same time, yet have totally different experiences.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This reduction of spontaneous, shared experiences have led to an erosion of the bonds that bind us together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MCCY will step up efforts to foster greater interaction, understanding and respect among Singaporeans, as this is what keeps our Singapore identity strong.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will do this through our strengths in arts, heritage, culture and sport, which form our identity infrastructure.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One of MCCY's priorities going forward is to deepen our multiculturalism, a core value that we all hold dearly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Over the years, MCCY has consistently invested in preserving and enhancing our multiculturalism.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our arts and heritage programmes, such as ArtsEverywhere@CDC and Heritage Activation Nodes, bring Singaporeans from different backgrounds together to appreciate and understand each other's heritage and culture better.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our Harmony Circles encourage honest conversations, build empathy, trust and respect across differences, so that we do not just live alongside one another, but we stand together and we celebrate each other's cultures and beliefs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I agree with Mr Mark Lee that we should set our ambitions higher, going beyond peaceful and harmonious co-existence, to foster deep cross-cultural understanding and appreciation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: When I speak with practitioners from our arts and culture groups, they tell me they are starting to notice declining interest among the young to engage in traditional arts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Some youths are trading traditional dance CCAs for contemporary dance styles, such as K-pop.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: So, while I understand the allure of K-pop and K-drama, we also need to retain our diverse traditional art forms and culture that forms the foundation for our multicultural identity and we need to pass these on to the next generation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: So, we will be stepping up our efforts to strengthen our unique multicultural identity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Minister of State Baey will elaborate on this.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Senior Minister of State Low and Minister of State Dinesh will elaborate further.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Through these initiatives, we want more Singaporeans to appreciate, experience and treasure the multicultural identity that makes us Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: On the community front, we will do more to share our unique multicultural identity with newcomers who choose to live, work and study in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Newcomers need to understand and appreciate that Singapore is not a homogeneous or monocultural society, and they have to adapt to a set of norms that may be different from where they came from.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At the same time, Singaporeans also need to make a conscious effort to share our culture, values and norms with them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The second is to encourage people to care for one another and contribute to building Singapore together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: While activities bring people together, it is care and connection that keeps us together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This spirit of care is alive and well in our society – we saw this clearly during COVID-19 when people instinctively stepped up in their own different ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We continue to see it in everyday acts, such as giving up our seats to people who need them more than us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our ambition is to build a vibrant and thriving democracy of deeds, where more Singaporeans can contribute to build Singapore together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At 60, a breast cancer survivor, Ms Yu discovered the benefits of water exercise during her rehabilitation and was driven to share this gift.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: She created bite-sized aqua-fitness videos and led twelve classes for seniors from Fei Yue Active Ageing Centre.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The seniors enjoyed the sessions so much that they encouraged Ms Yu to offer these classes more regularly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We want to lower barriers and create more opportunities for Singaporeans, like Ms Yu, to step forward to contribute.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In 2016, we launched Our Singapore Fund to partner citizens and turn their ideas for the community into reality.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: While Our Singapore Fund is very well received and has made a real impact on the ground, there are pain points.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, the grant cap and short implementation period confined projects; and the need to co-fund posed challenges for smaller ground-up groups or individuals who lacked fundraising capability.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This fund supports bigger projects and dreams, welcomes smaller groups and embraces good ideas wherever they come from.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Senior Minister of State Low will share more on how this will work.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We want to empower more Singaporeans to contribute meaningfully, so we can build stronger bonds, deeper trust and a greater sense of shared ownership.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is the first step towards building a stronger "we first" society.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our strength lies in our diversity of talents – from entrepreneurs to artists.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: When we create pathways that allow Singaporeans to pursue their passion and thrive in their chosen fields, we forge a strong national identity built on the shared belief that every Singaporean matters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is especially important for our youths, who will have to overcome new challenges in this uncertain AI-dominated and changed world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As Ms Elysa Chen, Prof Kenneth Poon and Mr Alex Yam pointed out, our youths increasingly struggle with social isolation, worsening mental health outcomes and growing career insecurities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The National Youth Council (NYC) is committed to support our young people to make them active participants equipped with the skills, opportunities and support systems to thrive and fulfil their aspirations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh will share more about our initiatives in this area.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Sport is a powerful unifier for all Singaporeans, transcending age and ability.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Sport also ignites national pride and solidifies our national identity, as Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh pointed out.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MCCY and SportSG will step up efforts to further democratise sports participation among youths.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I share Mr Alex Yam's concerns that sport CCAs should not be something only for the naturally gifted or those who can afford prior training.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will provide more platforms where children can play to nurture their love of the game – so that every child has more opportunities to experience what sport can teach them about themselves and others.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We introduced the School Sports Fiesta last year to bring students from different schools together to play sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To date, we have held Fiestas for 16 schools and well over 2,000 students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Fifteen-year-old Aryaa Geajaindren from St Gabriel's Secondary School had never considered playing basketball.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The School Sports Fiesta sparked a desire in him to explore the sport more deeply.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Another platform is through CCAs, where students train together, forging bonds through sweat, blood and tears.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: CCAs are where many of us made our closest friends, forged through hours spent laughing and crying together in training.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This sustained interaction and tight bonds is precisely what we want to nurture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will launch more in the next few years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As a ground-up initiative, some schools have also come together to form Multi-School CCA Teams.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, ACS (Barker Road) and Queensway Secondary came together to form a hockey team that trained together and competed together at the National School Games (NSG).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This year will see its highest participation to date, with around 69,000 student-athletes from more than 300 schools competing across 29 sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We want to expand this to provide more opportunities for our student-athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MCCY and MOE will start a new initiative to work with ready, able and willing NSAs to introduce more sports into the NSG.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The power of sport to unite and build connections goes beyond schools.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The friendships forged through playing together, the encouragement shared during a challenging game and the growth that comes from pushing our limits.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These are experiences that all Singaporeans, regardless of age and ability, should continue to have access to throughout their lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Therefore, SportSG will also step up our efforts to democratise sports in the community and ensure that everyone can continue to bond and to live better through sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Gho Sze Kee will be glad to hear that we have been steadily expanding sport spaces, especially in the heartlands.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have renovated four sport facilities, such as the Delta Sport Centre and the ActiveSG Sport Park @ Teck Ghee, and completed 15 development projects, including Bukit Canberra and the ActiveSG Sport Village @ Jurong Town.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Within a year, we will be completing three facilities to provide more localised sport access.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They are Queenstown, Hougang and the new Punggol Regional Sport Centre.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have also completed 11 Sport-in-Precinct facilities with another 11 undergoing construction in Tampines North, Keat Hong, Whampoa and Kembangan, amongst others.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our facilities are well-utilised and see over 20 million visitors annually.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This includes the recently opened eight dual-use pickleball courts at The Kallang and we will soon complete another eight pickleball courts at the Little India Bus Terminal.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As we build these new courts, we are mindful of managing noise levels at residential estates.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I commend Ms Gho Sze Kee's efforts in arbitrating citizen considerations and pushing for foam balls that are quieter in her ward.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG will work with community stakeholders on solutions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And where it meets space and height requirements, we will also activate underutilised spaces, such as spaces under viaducts in our neighbourhoods, so that these facilities are conveniently located closer to Singaporeans, but far enough to manage noise levels.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We can see an example like the Gali Batu flyover.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I hope this addresses Ms Goh Sze Kee's concerns and I also hope that this is more than a 80% solution.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, the issue with the MND is not about revenue loss, but it is about whether residents are well served, especially noise, as many multi-storey car parks are located very close to flats.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I believe on 4 November, there was also a Parliamentary Question filed by Member Mr David Hoe, which received a comprehensive reply from MND on what the considerations were.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Perhaps I will point the Member to look up that Parliamentary Question reply.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They must follow with more programmes for all ages and abilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have ActiveSG Academies and Clubs, that are open to children and youths to play the sport they like.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Some go on to developmental programmes in high performance sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We also have ActiveSG Interest Groups and Learn-to-Play programmes for adults who wish to pick up a new sport or just to play recreationally.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are committed to offering more of such programmes and will study what Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh has mentioned about the SG Sport Pass.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Andre Low asked about access to strength training to combat ageing-related frailty.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have introduced the Frailty Prevention Programme (FPP) for seniors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This enables them to age healthily and continue to build social connections through sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Since then, CALM has yielded positive physical changes in our seniors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: After experiencing a stroke in 2025, she joined CALM 1.0.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Under the guidance of her trainer, Ms Florence gradually regained her strength, mobility and flexibility, including improvements in her breathing and mood.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This experience is not just unique to Ms Florence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In fact, almost all CALM participants reported improved functional performance in at least one measure, such as handgrip strength or gait speed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Besides CALM, our seniors have also found adaptive sport attractive and useful in keeping them active, healthy and socially connected, whether it is through seated floorball or disc golf.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As part of the FPP, SportSG has progressively equipped 200 AACs with adaptive sport equipment.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: By the end of 2026, we will target to equip all AACs so that more seniors can participate in adaptive sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Low will also be glad to know that at the end of the CALM programme, participants are introduced to HUR machines.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Almost all Senior Care Centres and some AACs are equipped with these variable weight machines.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Last year, we also launched the Seniors National Games (SNG), where seniors represented their AACs to compete across five adaptive sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are heartened by the turnout – over 4,500 seniors from 110 AACs and even more family, friends and fans – and the positive feedback on how the SNG provided opportunities for seniors to not only keep active but also build connections and have fun.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We invite more seniors to take part this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For persons with disabilities, we launched the Enabling Sports Fund (ESF) last year, supported by the President's Challenge and as part of the refreshed Disability Sports Master Plan to support community-initiated projects.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One of these is from SUN-DAC, which created iBoccia, a modification of the Paralympic sport, Boccia. iBoccia is customised and suitable for both persons with intellectual or other disabilities and their able-bodied teammates.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Through the Fund, SUN-DAC will introduce iBoccia to more persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Sport also opens doors for Singaporeans to chase their dreams.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: With the right support, we believe our athletes can realise their aspirations and their full potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked for an update on athlete support.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have put in place spexPotential to nurture athletes with potential for gold medal success at the Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have increased stipends and introduced Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups for our spexScholars to make competitive sport more financially viable.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We signed agreements with six autonomous universities to create more athlete-friendly environments and launched the spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships for athletes to pursue both education and competitive sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Take for example, Ryan Lo, a gold medallist at the Asian Games 2023 and last year's SEA Games and two-time Olympian sailor.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The spexEducation Programme Office worked closely with James Cook University to balance his academic commitments with training and competitions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: He is on track to complete his business degree with a shorter duration, enabling him to pursue both his sporting ambitions and educational aspirations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ryan will also be defending his title at this years' Asian Games, so let us cheer him on.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, we will enhance the breadth and depth of our support to athletes by making our high performance sports system more athlete-centric and whole-of-life.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To enable more of our athletes to stay longer and go further in sport, we will support them with specialist expertise and in managing sporting commitments and other demands of life.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our athlete life performance managers have commenced personalised consultations with top athletes, co-developing plans to help them manage major life transitions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh will be glad to know that we will also run workshops to equip our athletes with skills in areas, such as personal branding, entrepreneurship, mental wellness literacy and media training.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will also deepen and integrate sport science and sport medicine (SSSM) support for our athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: A key benefit of the consolidation is the pooling of our SSSM expertise and knowledge.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This will increase our capacity and open more opportunities for cross-knowledge transfer and pathways for career progression.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our athletes will see more dedicated and consistent support across sports and, as a system, we reap synergies that we otherwise would not if the entities remain separated.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, within SpexSG, we will strengthen SSP's role as our education concierge for all Team Singapore student-athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, SSP provides a dedicated high-performance developmental pathway for youth athletes at the secondary and post-secondary levels.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SSP currently avails its annual University and Scholarship Fair and university advisory services to Team Singapore student-athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Going ahead, it will support Team Singapore student-athletes in all six of our local autonomous universities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SSP is also developing capabilities to support overseas-based Team Singapore student-athletes so that they can learn with their SSP classmates in Singapore for both the secondary and the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SSP will further enhance its partnerships with NSAs and lean forward with boarding and facilities support.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One example is the Junior Performance Pathway Programme, a collaboration between SSP and the Singapore Badminton Association.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Under this programme, student-athletes who are not studying at SSP can access training sessions at SSP and they can also board with SSP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SSP will continue to develop such partnerships with more NSAs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Altogether, these changes will enable our student-athletes to pursue their aspirations and realise their full potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Third, SpexSG will tighten integration with our NSAs, empowering them to develop their sport for excellence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Like Mr Jackson Lam, I too hear from NSAs their aspirations and challenges.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will strengthen our support for and partnerships with the NSAs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For new and emerging NSAs, we will also develop a playbook to guide them in achieving Charity status.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will also have media communication trainings for NSAs to enhance media management capabilities and athlete profiling efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SpexSG will also expand secondment opportunities for sport administrators to more NSAs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, SportSG seconds chief executive officers, general managers and high performance managers to NSAs, such as Sailing, Fencing and Badminton.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I hope Mr Jackson Lam and Ms Valerie Lee will be happy with these changes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: But above all, SpexSG will transform the end-to-end journey of our national athletes to be a lot more integrated and seamless.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The 3x3 basketball is gaining popularity because of its high-intensity and fast-paced game play.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our men's and women's team are both ranked top six in Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The National Youth teams come together for a few months before major competitions and then, they separate after that.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This ad hoc training environment does not develop their technical skill, decision-making speed and high-performance habits to their full potential, neither does it build team chemistry.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: How does this look like for an athlete?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Emily Elessa is a high potential talent in the national Under-16 girls' team that won a silver medal in the Under-16 Southeast Asia Basketball Association qualifiers last year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Recently, she decided to transfer from her Direct School Admission (DSA) school, Yishun Secondary School, to SSP to pursue her aspiration to represent Singapore at the senior level.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This consistency means that Emily is building the right technical, physical and mental foundations for progression into the senior national team.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Emily will also now have year-round sport science and sport medicine support.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Beyond sport, Emily will also be able to build a strong academic foundation in SSP, with all the flexibility that Team Singapore athletes need.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: She will also have access to the suite of Athlete Life Management offerings where she can seek guidance for her other life priorities so she can be ready for life.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: After 60 years of nation building, we have bonded over our shared experience, built a strong multicultural community that will step up to drive positive change.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We forged a united society that identifies ourselves first as Singaporeans and not by our race, language or religion.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Faced again with the uncertainty of a changed world, let us stand on the shoulders of our Pioneers and choose to build an even more cohesive and stronger Singapore, one where our ethnic and religious communities not only live in harmony, but share a deep appreciation for one another's culture, one where everyone contributes actively to care for and uplift others in our community, one where everyone can fulfil their aspirations and reach their full potential, one that is truly a "we first" society.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Mark Lee asked what success looks like.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Chairman, I believe it is the Singapore that Mr S Rajaratnam envisioned as he wrote our pledge 60 years ago – where we come together to celebrate our diverse cultures and share the same "we first" values, where we choose to be united as one people, trust each other, uplift one another, give back to society and where everyone can succeed on their own terms, where we cast aside our differences in race, language or religion; and we contribute in our own way to build our nation, where every Singaporean, regardless of their starting point, can achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Let us come together and work towards this dream just like how our forefathers did when Mr S Rajaratnam first wrote our pledge.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Let us not be mere spectators, but pledge ourselves as one united people, so that we can achieve happiness, prosperity and progress for our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, I recently visited the Founders' Memorial's "Not Mere Spectators" exhibition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since 1959, Singapore's diversity has been built and held together by our people's active participation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Throughout the years, Singaporeans stepped forward to care for one another and uphold our unity in diversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These were performances by the people, for the people, nurturing a sense of belonging, mutual respect and shared identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Held in open spaces across Singapore, people came together to perform, watch and learn together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Several Pioneers in our arts scene, like Dr Uma Rajan and Mdm Som Said, performed at these concerts and became lifelong friends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Their experiences at these concerts left them with a deep conviction that multiculturalism must be lived and not just be spoken about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Both, in fact, went on to shape Singapore's cultural landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our nation's early years and journey reflect the seeds and the foundation of the "we first" society that we seek to forge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We see this "we first" spirit at different levels of our society where Singaporeans care, share and uplift each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the individual level, we see it in volunteers, like Mdm Ratnam Periowsamy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At 90, she is the oldest volunteer at Care Corner's AAC in Toa Payoh East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: She goes door-to-door to check on seniors living alone and organises activities for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Her example shows us that you can contribute and care, regardless of age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the community level, groups, like the Kampong Gelam Association, came together to develop the Kampong Gelam Place Plan to enhance the precinct's heritage and cultural importance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the business level, we see the "we first" spirit in companies like aAdvantage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: About half of their 20 staff members receive time off to volunteer regularly at a nursing home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, the common thread that we shared earlier at the individual, business and community levels show ordinary Singaporeans and groups stepping forward to make a difference, a big impact on our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is the kind of "we first" spirit that MCCY seeks to spark, spur and strengthen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will do so by, number one, creating common spaces through our heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will bring people together, both physically and in spirit, to foster a stronger sense of community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And number two, by encouraging and enabling active citizenry to ensure that good ideas are turned into actions and no one is left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, when we speak about heritage as a common space, we are referring not only to our landmarks, but also to familiar places within our neighbourhoods – places that hold meaning, memory and shared experience among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Foo Cexiang asked about MCCY's plan to allow more Singaporeans to play an active role in celebrating our neighbourhood heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the NHB's Heritage Activation Nodes (HANs), NHB partners residents and stakeholders to co-create programmes celebrating their neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They are in Katong-Joo Chiat, Clementi and Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In Katong-Joo Chiat, there is a mural of a mama shop along Lorong Stangee, created by local artist Mr Alvin Mark Tan based on his childhood memories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This mural has inspired passers-by to contribute their stories and old photos of Joo Chiat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One will be in Telok Blangah, in partnership with Participate in Design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will focus on uncovering hidden neighbourhood gems and stories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And the other HAN will be in Tiong Bahru, with Tiong Bahru Community Centre as our partner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will celebrate public housing architecture, religious sites as well as heritage businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will continue to steward our landmarks and historic districts carefully, so they remain meaningful to all Singaporeans and are sensitively integrated into the everyday lives of surrounding communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked for a whole-of-Government approach in assessing the future public use of 38 Oxley Road and to consult neighbouring residents throughout the decision-making process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As mentioned by Acting Minister David Neo in his previous Ministerial Statement, MCCY will certainly study possible options to make the site accessible to the public, so it can become part of our shared memory and a common space for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The acquisition process for the site is ongoing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Once access is obtained, NHB will conduct a holistic study in consultation with the relevant agencies, to assess how the public education value of the site can be optimised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will work with the Member, as well as the relevant Government agencies, to engage residents living nearby the site, and consider ideas and feedback to minimise any potential disamenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Project Office will work closely with key district stakeholders, like the Kampong Gelam Association, Little India Shopkeepers and Heritage Association and Chinatown Business Association, to better understand their needs and empower them to enliven their precincts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Heritage businesses play an important role in enhancing the unique character of our historic districts and serve as community anchors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked whether more targeted succession planning support could be given to preserve heritage businesses and support their financial viability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that succession planning can be complex and deeply personal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Rumah Makan Minang, a third-generation family-run restaurant, tapped on this grant to strengthen its long-term sustainability by reviewing and restructuring roles within the family business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NHB will also be working with citizen volunteers to document heritage businesses and their contributions as part of the Little India Citizen Engagement Project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Interested members of the community can look out for NHB's call for citizen volunteers for the exercise, which will be announced by May this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These efforts remind us that heritage endures not only because it is preserved by institutions, but because it is kept alive by people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, besides strengthening our sense of community through heritage spaces, we will nurture the growth of a "we first" society by spurring active citizenry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to see everyone coming together to shape and take ownership of our shared future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To spark active citizenry, we set up the Singapore Government Partnerships Office two years ago in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, the Government received more than 1,600 partnership proposals addressing a wide range of community needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is a youth-led performing arts ground-up with the mission to connect people through performances in public spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During SG60, they staged more than 20 performances across five locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another project is Skillseed, an established community builder that works with residents to uncover neighbourhood stories and to strengthen local leadership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Skillseed seeks to build trust, capability and ownership within the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Both projects had different starting points, but they have the same spirit of contribution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Such citizen-driven initiatives have immense potential to spread their impact and outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That is where the new SG Partnerships Fund announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and just now by Acting Minister David Neo, will play a key role to spur and strengthen active citizenry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As requested by Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, I will briefly share how the fund is tailored.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is tailored to empower different levels of ground-up ideas and activities through three tiers of support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope that this tier, with its simple application process, will motivate more individuals and ground-ups to come forward with their ideas, no matter how small, to address community needs or to better the lives of fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The next tier, the Sprout tier, aims to grow the circle of ground action by providing support for those with proven ideas to amplify their impact and outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is also the next tier of funding that successful "graduates" of Seed tier recipients could apply to, to grow their project ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This can take the form of large-scale initiatives that grow civic participation or capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Similar to Sprout, applicants for this tier would need to demonstrate prior success in implementing projects of similar nature and that the proposed idea has achieved tangible results in pilots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, we recognise that implementing such programmes could require greater capacity from the organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, we will work with successful Scale applicants, to strengthen their capabilities to execute their projects more sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The fund will also cover capacity costs, such as manpower and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We wish to ensure that it remains accessible to encourage a broad range of initiatives that leads to positive change for our communities, certainly including youths and certainly including parents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The SG Partnerships Fund also complements existing schemes, such as the NYC's Young ChangeMakers Grant and the National Youth Fund (NYF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure her that we will review the SG Partnerships Fund's impact on catalysing projects that support active citizenry, before we consider enlarging it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Applications will open from next month, April 2026, and more information will be released on the Singapore Government Partnerships Office's website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We welcome and we invite all Singaporeans to step forward and make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Your ideas and efforts matter, and we can create a "we first" Singapore where no one walks alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, a "we first" society is built when people, communities and businesses step forward to serve the collective good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim has asked how we can rally more to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will incentivise and actively support corporate volunteerism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will help companies build capability and confidence to contribute and shape our society for the better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, the partnership between the Singapore Business Federation and VolunteerInc. provides companies with training, guidance and connections to community organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since the programme was launched in July last year, more than 100 companies have stepped forward to partner VolunteerInc.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of them is, Coface, a multinational trade credit insurance company, which launched a drive to develop adaptive floorball sessions for elderly persons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, 52 Coface volunteers contributed 624 hours of their time over eight floorball sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this very meaningful initiative saw the seniors gain confidence through adaptive floorball; form friendships not just amongst the elderly, and also with the Coface employees; and rediscover the joy of staying active.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, we will continue to nurture a culture of giving back.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2025, under the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre's Company of Good initiative recognised 371 companies for their contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Then there is the Collective for a Stronger Society, launched two years ago, in 2024, and led by the Community Foundation of Singapore, which brings together Government agencies, donors and community partners to better support lower-income families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Elysa Chen asked whether the Government is considering alternative ways to encourage neighbourliness and mutual help, for example, through time-banking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While time banking is a good idea to increase neighbourliness and foster mutual help, there may be practical implementation challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, I want to assure her that there are community-led initiatives that have similar objectives to time banking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Thye Hua Kwan's Moral Charities implemented a programme, supported by the DBS Foundation, where AAC participants take on short micro-tasks based on their abilities and schedules, and receive small allowances upon completion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure her that MCCY will be happy to support similar ground-up initiatives, including any time-banking pilots, under the just-announced SG Partnerships Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, while corporate and organised giving matter greatly, a "we first" society is also expressed through everyday acts of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Volunteerism, therefore, is vital to growing active citizenry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our island-wide network of 24 SG Cares Volunteer Centres works closely with communities to identify and address their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More than 720 volunteers from semiconductor manufacturer, Micron, partnered with the SG Cares Volunteer Centre in Sembawang to run Micron Kampong, which befriends seniors and brings them on outings and festive visits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we aim to engage 36,000 volunteers to benefit 180,000 service users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: When corporates, community groups, and individuals choose to step forward, to connect, to care and to contribute, the foundations of active citizenry are built and the seeds for a "we first" society are sown.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, the foundation of Singapore's nation-building is the establishment of a harmonious and prosperous multiracial and multicultural society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We often say, "First, the nation; then the home" – first "we"; then "me".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The core tenet of prioritising "we" over "me" is the foundation upon which Singapore relies for survival and prosperity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To deepen our sense of "we first", we hope to adopt a three-pronged approach through "business", "community" and "individuals" to strengthen mutual care and build a "we first" society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, the Government will continue to harness our heritage and culture to create more common spaces to strengthen social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NHB will establish a Placemaking Project Office to work with businesses, associations and individuals within the community to enliven our historic districts and strengthen Singaporeans' sense of identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also add on to our existing three Heritage Activation Nodes with the introduction of two new Nodes in Telok Blangah and Tiong Bahru, which are both neighbourhoods rich in history and culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: From the "Seed" stage with an annual cap of $5,000, to the "Sprout" stage with up to $50,000 up to a period of two years, to the "Scale" stage with up to $1 million over three years, the Government hopes to encourage individuals and organisations to start small and share more creative good ideas with more people to unite the community through progressive support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us shape a "we first" Singapore, strong and resilient, and stronger together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, Acting Minister spoke about how multiculturalism bridges communities and forms the core of who we are as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Multiculturalism is and has always been, the bedrock of the Singapore identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For Singapore, a sense of shared identity is essential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It holds us together and gives us a sense of belonging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our multicultural identity reminds us of what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Today, we embrace it as a way of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This was on display just recently, when Chinese New Year coincided with the start of Ramadan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last Saturday afternoon in my constituency, I saw Muslim residents doing the lohei together with the community at a Chinese New Year celebration and grassroot leaders dabaoing the buffet, so that they can enjoy it after breaking fast.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even so, there is more that we can do and should do to deepen our multicultural DNA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Around the world, we see how social diversity leads to fragmentation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is therefore critical that we strengthen our cross-cultural understanding and deepen our shared identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is where the arts can be a powerful catalyst.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through the arts, we get to know ourselves and where we came from.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More importantly, arts encourage us to look beyond their differences and value our commonalities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is encouraging that in the Population Survey on the Arts, conducted by the NAC, eight in 10 Singaporeans agreed that the arts allow us to better understand people from different backgrounds and cultures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the years, the local arts scene has developed generations of practitioners, groups and platforms that embody Singapore's diverse cultural traditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Two weeks ago, I attended the Spring Reception held at the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One of the performances was a multi-ethnic percussive showcase.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Drum Feng opened the performance with Chinese drums, which was then joined by Nadi Singapura's kompang and rebana drums, and Singapore Dhol Squad's parai drums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These instruments from different cultures blended seamlessly to deliver a great performance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to support our traditional arts and culture, so that this precious part of our cultural heritage is passed down to future generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Various artists and arts groups whom we have consulted gave us this advice to develop multiculturalism through and in the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must work harder to engage the young to understand and appreciate the cultural heritage within and across the various ethnic communities and to expand the reach of monocultural traditional art forms within the general population.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In particular, we should promote cross-cultural awareness and appreciation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: By building these bridges, we learn to better appreciate the culture and art forms outside our own ethnic community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Upon this strong foundation, we can do more to support cross-cultural artistic creations that are sophisticated, innovative, high quality and that are uniquely Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To achieve this, we will provide more support to promote the development of multicultural art forms, whether through productions that infuse the influences of other cultures, creations and organisations that express our multiculturalism, or artists learning a new cultural art form from another ethnic community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Ms Eileen Chong spoke about, fostering greater participation among the young is important for the long-term sustainability of the arts sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Early and meaningful engagement with our diverse arts traditions lays the foundation for our children and youths to appreciate one another's cultures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is expanding opportunities for students to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At the preschool level, NAC will commission artists and arts groups to develop offerings that enable sustained access to arts experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One of the programmes, designed with The Artground, focuses on multicultural arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The programme will feature Malay and Indian dance, Peranakan arts, traditional hand puppetry and Chinese Opera.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will pilot these programmes with selected preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This enrichment programme will allow students from different schools to learn about various ethnic dance forms together, then apply them in contemporary dance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The students will have a chance to audition for a final showcase at Super 24, a regional competition featuring dance groups from across Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will strengthen funding support for schools to bring in artists to deliver traditional and multicultural arts learning experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond schools, we will increase the exposure of multicultural arts in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have been doing this through ArtsEverywhere@CDC, which brings arts and cultural performances to our everyday spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, Sri Warisan Som Said Performing Arts presented a blend of traditional Malay art forms, with musicians playing the angklungs, dancers weaving melodies into stories and intricate wayang golek puppets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The initiative has reached audiences of more than 63,000 since its launch in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Looking ahead, we will focus on showcasing Singapore's multiculturalism through ArtsEverywhere@CDC in our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will introduce more traditional arts and cross-cultural performances and programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These will deepen Singaporeans' understanding and appreciation of the cultures and traditions of different ethnic communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For instance, the Open Score Project, co-founded by Gildon Choo, combines global ethnic musical cultures and pushes the boundaries of cross-cultural collaboration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As part of ArtsEverywhere@CDC, their ensemble performed at Jurong Lake Gardens last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through such programmes, we can grow a deeper appreciation for arts experiences that connect our cultures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to encourage even more arts practitioners and groups to nurture connections and collaborations that express who we are as a people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Grant will support artists and projects blending elements from different cultures, traditions and disciplines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This could support artists who interweave elements from different cultures in a meaningful way and those who wish to develop mastery in art forms beyond their own cultural traditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It will also support ecosystem-building activities that strengthen the multicultural arts landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Multicultural Arts Programme Grant will be launched in the coming months, and NAC will share more details then.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Another initiative that expands access to local arts and culture offerings is the SG Culture Pass, launched in September 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Among those who have used their credits, nine in 10 expressed interest to attend another local programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through the Culture Pass, Singaporeans have discovered more about different cultures in Singapore beyond their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the scheme was just launched recently, MCCY will monitor utilisation trends before making adjustments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Nevertheless, we are encouraged by the statistics, which show that the Culture Pass has helped Singaporeans discover the diversity of our local cultural landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Assoc Prof Terence Ho also asked about whether more could be done to support our local publishers and bookstores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This strengthens our support of the local literary arts sector and directly benefits publishers and bookstores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Besides expanding access to the arts and developing audiences, we are exploring ways to harness the potential of the arts to generate positive social impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One such area is in arts education research.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Positive engagement with the arts from a young age supports holistic development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through sustained and localised research, we can better determine how arts-based education can nurture the next generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY has commissioned a five-year research study on how arts engagement can boost creativity and strengthen the socio-emotional well-being of our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The study is led by the National Institute of Education, in partnership with MCCY, NAC and the Esplanade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through this study, we hope to provide insights for schools and arts agencies that inform efforts to support youth development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Another emerging area that shows great promise is the nexus of arts and well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The National Gallery Singapore's Slow Art Guide is an example, delivered through a self-guided audio experience and reflection booklets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through slow looking and mindfulness exercises, the initiative encourages visitors to engage mindfully with artworks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This evidence-based approach positively impacts mental health and cognitive function.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Singapore's population ages, the arts provide a platform for our seniors to live and age well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC has partnered SingHealth Community Hospitals and the Agency for Integrated Care on a research study.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The study aims to determine the impact of arts programmes on senior well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The insights will help design effective interventions to support our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is also working with the arts community and healthcare and community care practitioners on a series of arts programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These programmes are designed to enhance the well-being of seniors at AACs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Kenneth Goh and Ms Goh Sze Kee asked about how we are supporting our artists to build sustainable and resilient careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arts self-employed persons (SEPs) form a significant segment of Singapore's arts workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are committed to empowering them to build capabilities and forge meaningful careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is around two thirds of our arts SEPs in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: He went through the Arts Resource Hub's IGNITE programme, which provided mentorship, networks and guidance in building a brand identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Julian established Wushiren Theatre with his wife in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Their debut production, I Am Finally In Love With The World, was successfully staged in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We recognise that our arts SEPs face evolving challenges that require enhanced support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It will provide SEPs with education programmes and tailored resources to strengthen their understanding of legal topics and empower them to capitalise on opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SEPs can also tap on consultations with a dedicated onsite lawyer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These initiatives that I shared today ensure that we continue to have strong funding, talent and domestic support pipelines for the arts, which Ms Eileen Chong spoke about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As we support our artists and arts groups to thrive and express our cultural heritage, they serve as our ambassadors to the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh had asked about using cultural diplomacy to reinforce our Singapore identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to support our practitioners to make their mark internationally and to showcase our Singapore identity beyond our shores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For instance, the Singapore Pavilion at the Osaka World Expo 2025 featured many local performing artists, including multicultural ensemble yINHarmony, acapella group The Island Voices and Bharathanatyam dancer Shruthi Nair, showcasing Singapore's rich cultural diversity to global visitors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, as we look ahead, Singapore must prepare to face new waves of challenges from a changing world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
