text: Strengthening our shared identity will enable us to overcome these challenges with confidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The arts have the unique power to deepen our distinctive brand of multiculturalism and build a more inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to invest in and grow the arts landscape to amplify its positive impact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Across Singapore, communities celebrate one another's cultures, from the multicultural floats at the Chingay parade to the annual iftar at Khadijah Mosque where I sat alongside religious leaders from the Inter-Religious Organisation (IRO) to break fast.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is a rare sight in today's world, where trust is in short supply and where multiculturalism is in retreat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We have seen this in the years before Independence, during the hardships of the second World War and when communal tensions were high.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Yet, even when the odds were stacked against us, our Pioneer religious leaders chose unity and harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This exemplifies Singapore's approach to social cohesion, one where people from different backgrounds make an active effort to appreciate each other's cultures and traditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The mission to build a strong, cohesive and caring society is an ongoing one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: First, to build strong communities with a shared cultural identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Second, to deepen the understanding between communities and to expand our common spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Third, to architect an ecosystem of care and mutual help so as to uplift all communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Early generations brought languages, traditions and beliefs from their home countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They provided mutual assistance as they settled in Singapore, forming associations and clans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Over time, new generations came of age and more took root here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: While we have kept our racial and religious identities, our practices have evolved to become uniquely Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: It is important that we steward our cultural heritage so that future generations can understand who we are and where we come from.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I hope this is useful, especially to our youths, including those from the East Coast Internship Programme, who are joining us here today in the gallery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Assoc Prof Faishal spoke about the Malay Heritage Centre earlier and Senior Minister of State Low about enlivening our historic districts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our goal is to help Singaporeans and international visitors understand and appreciate Singaporean Indian cultures and customs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our efforts to build a strong Indian community will go beyond culture and heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Last year, Minister Shanmugam announced that Senior Minister of State Murali Pillai and myself will lead a new committee to take the Indian community forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: More than 150 Singapore Indian organisations have shared their aspirations and ideas, particularly on how we could uplift members of our community together and to integrate more strongly as one united Indian community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This will be a committee by the community and for the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Its aim is to build strong networks across the Indian community, bringing together partners who are already doing good work on the ground, including SINDA and Narpani.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: First, to improve socioeconomic outcomes for the Indian community, particularly the vulnerable and the disadvantaged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Second, to champion integration and unity among the Indian community in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will have the first dialogue in April 2026, with the theme of building a strong and united Indian community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will also configure sub-committees and I invite members of the community to step forward, share your perspectives and play an active role in shaping this important initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: More details will be announced at the dialogue in April.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Tamil. :   Last August, the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs Shanmugam announced a new committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This committee, which is co-chaired by Senior Minister of State Murali and myself, will take the Indian community forward over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Since the announcement, we have held discussions with members from various segments of our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Participants shared their thoughts on the challenges faced by the Indian community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Their views were centred around the common themes of social cohesion and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This committee will take the excellent work being carried out by community organisations, including SINDA and Narpani, to the next level.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We also believe in developing skills among the next generation of leaders and identifying new talents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In addition, I am pleased to announce that we will hold an annual forum to discuss matters important to our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We plan to hold the first dialogue in April 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: More details about the INEI committee will be shared then.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I request members of the community to come forward and share their views. : Let me now move to the second area of deepening understanding between communities and expanding our common spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I spoke earlier about global uncertainties, and Singapore is not immune to these developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The Serangoon and Cashew Harmony Circles rallied neighbouring religious organisations to offer support and reassurance to the affected communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our apex religious organisations put out public statements of solidarity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Their message to the public was clear – an attack on one community is an attack on all communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Each incident is an opportunity to build up our reservoirs of trust so that we can stand united in troubled times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: That is why we continue to invest in our Racial and Religious Harmony Circles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This included the first youth-led intercultural showcase called Kaleidoscope: Harmony in Motion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This year, we will step up our efforts to engage religious organisations and build an even stronger inter-faith network in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Mr Chairman, our ability to foster unity and inclusivity amidst diversity is Singapore's enduring competitive advantage to attract international businesses and talents here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: But as I said earlier, our model of multiculturalism is unique and some newcomers may take more time to adapt to it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: After all, integration is a two-way street, which will require locals to be receptive and newcomers to make the effort to understand our culture, values and norms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The workplace is a natural space for this interaction to take place meaningfully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As mentioned by Acting Minister David Neo, the Alliance for Action (AfA) on the Integration of Foreign Professionals had conducted extensive engagements to develop practical solutions that industry partners can adopt to integrate foreign professionals at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: In the coming months, the Government will roll out new orientation and onboarding programmes for our EP holders, with a focus on workplace and living norms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: These will complement existing programmes for New Citizens and for our Permanent Residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The Singapore National Employers Federation and the Singapore Business Federation will also launch new resources for firms, including a Workplace Integration Playbook and a new cultural intelligence and sensitivity training course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: I am pleased to share that five trade associations and chambers have come onboard to roll out Orientation Day programmes for new EP holders, which will introduce them to our workplace norms and provide them with opportunities to network with their Singaporean counterparts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This will be scaled up to more trade associations and chambers over time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The third area I will speak on is to architect an ecosystem of care that every community can tap on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Our co-operatives (co-ops) are one of the oldest forms of community mutual help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: They are defined not by identity, but by a common purpose.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Since 1925, our co-ops have played a vital role to meet the evolving needs of our people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Some may be familiar with credit co-ops, which provide thrift and loan services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: There are also consumer and services co-ops, like the Silver Caregivers Co-operative, which provides community support for caregivers and equips them with skills, such as managing palliative care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: However, as Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari had earlier noted, our co-ops are facing growing challenges to renew their talent pipeline and to attract young members in a more competitive landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This is why MCCY announced the Co-op 10-year Transformation Roadmap in 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: This Roadmap will nurture a forward-looking sector that is purposeful, professional and trusted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: We will help co-ops stay relevant as they develop new capabilities to address emerging needs and transform for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: Co-ops will receive support to invest in talent development, governance and operational efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: As part of the Roadmap, MCCY and the Singapore National Co-operative Federation will jointly introduce the Co-operative Leaders Programme and Emerging Leaders Programme from this year, to develop the next generation of leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
text: The Roadmap also includes the Community Outreach and Impact Programme, which will provide seed funding, incubation spaces and mentorship for our youths to pilot innovative ideas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: What would you do, if you were not afraid?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I want to ask this of the young people who may be watching the COS today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But it is also a question for all of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: If fear was not holding you back, what would you try?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For many young people today, fear does not come from the lack of ability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It comes from growing up in a world that is highly connected and where missteps and comparisons are amplified.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But fear is an integral part of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our responsibility is therefore to ensure that our young people are equipped to meet it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And such courage does not happen in isolation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Courage grows when people feel supported, feel rooted and feel like they are part of something larger than themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Across many societies, we are seeing signs of weakening relationships and commitments that once anchored people to their communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Some observers describe this as a broad social drift towards detachment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ultimately, young people, like us all, want connection and purpose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: How can we empower our young people on their journey to find a sense of belonging, meaning and a sense of self, even as social bonds seemingly wane around the world?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: To answer this question, we went to our young people directly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Alex Yam, Prof Kenneth Poon, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim and other Members, advocated for the need to better engage our youths, to support them, and asked what more can we do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Like Members, MCCY strongly believes in this need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: What I will share today are some key areas we are developing under the SG Youth Plan to support different phases of a young person's life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When we listened carefully, what came through clearly was this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Early on, young people want the confidence to try, to test themselves, to fall and to get back up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They understand that the world is full of uncertainty, but they do not want to be sheltered from these challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They want real experiences, in the real world, with real people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As young people grow older, the questions shift to finding direction and meaning in work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And later still, many want to step forward, to contribute and shape the spaces and communities around them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But it all begins with the same question: do I have the courage to try?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It is not about leisure or being frivolous.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For young people, play is where you learn how to make mistakes, bounce back and how to do it with friends and family beside you.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When my daughter learned to rollerblade, her first lesson was not how to go fast.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And she had the most fun when learning with her friends – fumbling, laughing and getting back up together, made it easier to keep going.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Today, young people are spending more time online, but many crave real-life connections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When you head outdoors, especially to new places with new people, you discover something important.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Last year, about 18,000 students went through the MOC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In time, all 15-year-olds in Singapore will get to experience OBS at least once in their lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Each OBS watch comprises 12 students from different schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Strangers who will embark on the outdoors for five days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Through these shared experiences, they will learn life skills, gain confidence in tackling the unknown and make lasting friendships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Like Ms Valerie Lee, I am sure OBS has left a lasting impact on some in this Chamber.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In fact, I was in the same watch as Valerie when we were 15.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We went away sunburnt with legs full of sandfly bites, but the core memories stayed with us even till today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I am glad to update that the campus will open its doors later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Picture this, teams of four students working together on advanced rope challenges instead of just pairs today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: These expanded team activities will push more young people to rely on each other, building stronger bonds and greater resilience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: What is particularly meaningful is that some of these challenges, including high elements, will be wheelchair-accessible – this ensures that no student is left behind when acquiring and building these crucial life skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As Mr Darryl David reminded us, OBS was set up in 1967 by Dr Goh Keng Swee "to develop mentally and physically rugged youths to be active citizens inspired to serve the community." The words "rugged" and "active citizens" capture the evergreen spirit of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our eternal way of being, so that our nation endures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In 1967, we needed ruggedness as we struggled for nationhood.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Today, we need resilience to navigate an uncertain world and maintain a strong sense of identity and belonging as one people, one nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Darryl David and Ms Valerie Lee asked about extending OBS to all ages and expanding the OBS overseas programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Yet with finite resources, our priority must be to get the MOC scale-up right for our students first, before we consider other areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ms Valerie Lee also talked about supporting the Outdoor Adventure Education sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We have been doing so through the Outdoor Adventure Education Council, which was formed in 2022 to uplift the sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The Council brings partners together to establish national standards and exchange best practices across the sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Beyond organised activities, such as OBS, friendships form in ordinary moments of just being together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Many young people feel that as years pass, there are fewer physical places where this can happen naturally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Meanwhile, exciting programmes and activities are already happening at the Belt.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We relaunched *SCAPE last November and it is now a hive of activities centred on youth interests – anime, dance, art, tabletop games, music, the list goes on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I was at *SCAPE on a Friday evening and spoke to some of the young people hanging out there.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is what they told me, "It is a sandbox where I could quickly test my event concept." "Separately, in other places, we might get stares.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But here, there is no judgement." "This is a place to just be.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It gives us the time and space to pursue our ideas and passion." There was a palpable sense of hope and energy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And we are only four months into the relaunch. *SCAPE is just the start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We want to bring this movement closer to where our young people live.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will create more welcoming, open spaces across Singapore, where you can gather freely and form friendships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will share more details at the launch of the SG Youth Plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As young people move into the next stage in life, the questions change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For students coming out of school, the next step is entering the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Over the past days, many in this Chamber have highlighted youth anxieties about work, especially in the face of AI.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Indeed, it is daunting finding work now when you can barely imagine what jobs will exist tomorrow, let alone plan a career.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: What matters then, is building the skills to thrive with technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our Ministries are working hard at this, as shared by my colleagues over the past few days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For example, our Institutes of Higher Learning will enhance their AI curriculum, while emphasising soft skills that will complement the use of AI.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For working youths, we will support them in learning AI-related skills, such as providing free access to premium AI tools, for those who take up selected AI training courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Fundamentally, the real power lies in how our young people choose to engage in these tools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Your generation – the digital- or even the AI-native generation – knows how to use these tools instinctively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As much as it has the potential to replace some junior-level tasks, it can equip you with the power to compress traditional learning curves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Your generation will teach us many things about AI and its possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But we are also here for you with our experiences and memories of navigating change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We need to tap on each other's strengths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This shared learning is precisely what young people have told us matters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Someone to help them make sense of all this uncertainty and find their inner strength.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Someone to remind them that life does not follow a straight line, but there always are ways to find solid ground beneath your feet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is why we will grow mentorship opportunities so that our youths will have someone to journey with them through the big and small "leaps" in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We know that finding a mentor is not easy when there is so much to keep up with in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As such, we want to lower the barriers and make professional connections more accessible for you.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are bringing mentorships directly to schools, where you are.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We recently partnered three polytechnics to create mentoring programmes under Mentoring SG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Just imagine if we all step up to contribute our experience, lend a listening ear and journey together with our young people through their life transitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is the culture that we can only create if we set aside time for our young people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is what we want to do under Mentoring SG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: After navigating the next "leap" in life, something shifts yet again for many young people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They do not just ask, "What should I do?", but also start asking, "What can I change?" Young people told us clearly that being heard is not the same as being trusted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Prof Kenneth Poon and Dr Charlene Chen as well as Ms Elysa Chen asked about how we are supporting youth participation to create a sense of belonging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This seed funding programme puts youths in charge from start to finish.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Young people do not just receive funding and mentorship; they are fully responsible for evaluating each other's proposals and giving advice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For impactful proposals, we are prepared to support them further.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: There are different programmes that youths can access, such as the National Youth Fund and the new SG Partnerships Fund that Senior Minister of State Low just touched on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In his Budget speech, the Prime Minister also mentioned the Youth Panels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Youth Panels work differently but with the same spirit – young people partner directly with Government agencies to shape policies they care about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In the first run, 120 youths rolled up their sleeves to tackle topics, like financial resilience and environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The next run of the Youth Panels launches later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The CoLab will take control of the Somerset Belt's programming and activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They will decide which spaces serve what purpose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Simply put, they will create the vibe that defines the Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This way, youths can transform Somerset Belt into a place that is truly, boldly theirs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Let us envision a space that breathes with youthful life – a place they have built and filled with their energy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are putting our belief in our young people into action – real investment, real decisions, real responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is us saying: we trust you to lead; show us the way.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Chairman, please let me say a few lines in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government places great importance on youth development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They are the future leaders of our nation and our country's hope.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We sometimes inadvertently compare youth with the previous generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: However, each generation of Singaporeans faces their own challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Our current generation of youth has their aspirations and possesses a strong sense of social mission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Rather than comparing them with the previous generation, we should give them space to express themselves freely, find their own path and discover their own strengths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We should also give them opportunities to develop interpersonal skills through play or to grow from failure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We welcome suggestions from all sectors of the society and encourage active participation from all. : Mr Chairman, growing up is not a straight line.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It begins with learning you are tougher than you think.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It continues with you finding your way without losing who you are.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And it grows into stepping forward to shape what comes next.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As I shared at the beginning of my speech, around the world, many societies are grappling with weakening bonds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Surely, we must do all we can to avoid that.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: If we put the right pieces in place, can we move in the right direction?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Can we build a generation that feels deeply connected to society?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: A generation that feels that Singapore is theirs and that they are Singapore's?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will keep building the right support around you.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: And we will keep creating spaces for you to lead.

text: Instead, MUIS monitors worship patterns closely on the ground.

text: So, as I said in my speech, it comes down to whether the location is suitable, meets the specifications.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If it comes to having to do a lot of mitigation just to make it work, then we have to ask ourselves whether this is the best use of Government funds.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: There was also another thrust to my cut, which is about making strength training more accessible to Singaporeans at large, and I wonder if the Minister has a response to my suggestion to leverage our existing fitness corners as a means of providing easy access to strength training for the rest of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I was under the impression that his original suggestion was meant for seniors, which is why the reply was that actually, for seniors, they require quite different machines.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: They require machines that ideally have pneumatic weights so that they can be increased at small increments, as opposed to the standard kind of weight machines that we have, and therefore, the HUR machines that are available at the majority of our Senior Care Centres.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: When it comes to general weight training for Singaporeans, with SportSG as well as the private gym landscape in Singapore taken together, I think Singaporeans have a lot of different possibilities and accesses to whether it is gym weight machines or otherwise.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: To the specific suggestion about weight machines and our constituencies as well as HDB fitness corners and all that, that is something that we have provision for in some areas.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It is also something we are looking at.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: The Acting Minister has mentioned about the IPS survey and the survey actually indicates that younger Singaporeans are more likely to report feelings of social isolation, and more than half say that they find it easier to interact online than face-to-face.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: But at the same time, museums around the world are evolving beyond quiet exhibition spaces into social venues, hosting after-hours programmes that combine arts, music and interactive activities to attract younger audiences.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether MCCY and NHB would consider piloting museum-after-dark programmes designed for young adults, perhaps working with the NYC to design formats that resonate with how young people socialise today?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I also want to assure the Member that this is something that we are continually looking at.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, instead of after dark, NYC has also done programmes overnight.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: They have brought youths to stay overnight at the National Museum of Singapore, the National Gallery of Singapore and Changi Airport.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, the short answer is yes, we are open to studying and considering it, especially in the context that we have an existential problem, maybe this will help bring up our total fertility rate.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Although you did not file a cut, you can ask your clarification.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am still a youth, so, thank you.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, I would like to declare my interest as the executive director for Chinatown Heritage Centre.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I understand that MCCY is developing placemaking initiatives in the locale of Kampong Gelam and Little India, with the hopes to activate spaces and support heritage businesses.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would also like to ask if the Ministry will therefore consider expanding the coordination and support to Chinatown?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second supplementary question is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the MOE-OBS Challenge Programme be implemented only in OBS campsites?

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I ask this because there are other campsites, like Changi Coast, Dairy Farm and Jalan Bahtera.

speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I am wondering if those other campsites will be utilised and whether OBS will be the only operator for the MOE-OBS Challenge, or will there be other private outdoor adventure companies be operating it as well?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Member Cai Yinzhou for the clarification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, the team is not confined only to MCCY and NHB, but also work across the whole-of-Government, including the economic agencies under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, for example, Enterprise Singapore and STB, to come together to support the businesses in the historic districts to strengthen their capabilities in placemaking.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One, to design to implement and to scale up the placemaking so that we can boost their vibrancy as well as to drive footfall to the three historic districts, including Chinatown, and we are working very closely with the Chinatown Business Association on that.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: Also, we want to highlight that the programme is also expeditionary in nature, so there will be certain locations that make use of nature and surroundings.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: In terms of the operators, OBS will be the main operator, or the only operator for MOC.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: There are other operators out there that conduct camps, but these would be more for school-run specific camps.

speaker: The Chairman
text: As there are no further clarifications, can I invite Mr Alex Yam if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: So, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
